Summary: Daniel saw 'one like the Son of man' coming with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of Days, receiving dominion, glory, and a kingdom that will never pass away.
JewishBackground: In Daniel 7, the Son of Man is a heavenly figure, distinct from the four beasts that represent earthly empires. In Second Temple literature, notably the Parables of Enoch, a Son of Man figure appears as a preexistent heavenly judge. Rabbinic reading varied: some identified the figure with Israel itself, others read it messianically. The title therefore carried both human and heavenly associations in first-century Judaism, which is why it could serve as a claim to more than ordinary humanity.
PointsToChrist: The site's reading is that Jesus deliberately took this title as his own — it is his most frequent self-designation in the Gospels — and that at his trial he joined Daniel 7 to Psalm 110, telling the high priest they would see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of power and coming on the clouds (Matthew 26:64). The Christian claim is that the heavenly figure of Daniel's vision is Jesus himself.
